# DARK TARGETS — the compile-fail allowlist, and it is a RATCHET, not a parking lot.
#
# A target listed here does not compile at HEAD. That means every #[test] in it is a
# falsifier that CANNOT FIRE, which is indistinguishable from a falsifier that always
# passes. THE READER IS `scripts/check-dark-targets.py`: it FAILS if a target goes dark
# and is not on this list, FAILS if a row here compiles again (delete it), and FAILS if
# the sweep was PRUNED so that neither question could honestly be answered.
#
# Format: one row per target, exactly as `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
# --keep-going --message-format=short` names it, minus the trailing error count:
#
#     <package> (<kind>[ "<name>"])
#
# ── ⚑ 2026-08-03: THIS RATCHET WAS THE ONE THAT COULD NOT FIRE ──────────────────────
# `commons-arbiter` and `confined-swarm` both stopped compiling at 522b9c763 (11:55,
# `content_commit` widened to `[CommitLane; 8]` in two of its four twins), stayed dark
# ~11h until f71f7f35e (23:04), are not on this list — and nothing said the word "dark".
# THREE independent silencers, each sufficient on its own, all measured:
#
#   1. A GATE BEHIND A RED GATE. The ratchet was step 7 of `clippy-correctness`, and
#      Actions stops a job at the first FAILED step. Step 6 (the correctness sweep) had
#      two standing `always return zero` hits, so steps 7/8/9 — ALL THREE sweeps over
#      this file — were skipped. Across every ci.yml run 08-01..08-03: EXECUTED 3,
#      SKIPPED 31. All five runs inside the dark window read `skipped`.
#      FIXED: `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` on all three sweep steps.
#
#   2. ITS GREEN BRANCH WAS UNREACHABLE. The inline reader stripped `file ` rows but not
#      `never-run ` rows, so `dark-known.txt` held 66 rows belonging to the THIRD sweep
#      and `comm` reported every one of them as "NO LONGER DARK". Measured by running
#      the old snippet against a clean log: 0 new, 66 stale, exit 1. On the 3 runs it
#      did execute it happened to die on a NEW row first, which hid this completely.
#      FIXED: the reader partitions on both prefixes, and has a self-test that says so.
#
#   3. THE LOWER BOUND BELOW WAS ADVICE TO A HUMAN, NOT A CHECK. See the ⚠⚠ note.
#      FIXED: the pruned cone is now DERIVED and the gate refuses to render a verdict
#      over an incomplete measurement.
#
# The lesson that generalises past this file: sweeps 2 and 3 were `scripts/check-*.py`
# from birth and so had rows in `scripts/local-gates.sh` and ran on any box. This one was
# inline YAML, so it could only ever run in the one place that had stopped reaching it,
# and holes 2 and 3 were invisible until it became code you could execute.
#
# ⚠ REPRODUCING LOCALLY REQUIRES `--keep-going`. A plain `cargo clippy --all-targets`
# ABORTS at the first non-compiling target and shows you nothing past it — which is the
# whole reason twelve of these accumulated unseen through 2026-07-25.
#
# ⚠⚠ AND `--keep-going` IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. A red LIBRARY prunes its entire
# downstream cone: cargo cannot attempt anything that depends on a crate it failed to
# build. On 2026-07-25 `starbridge-v2`'s lib had been red since 07-17, and `dregg-persist`
# depends on it, so the first `--keep-going` sweep produced 711 lines and stopped well
# short of the workspace; the sweep AFTER that one lib was repaired produced 1775 and
# found four more dark targets, two of them (`ugc-dregg`, `dregg-perf`) months old.
# A dark-target count taken while ANY lib is red is a LOWER BOUND. Fix libs first, sweep
# again, and do not believe the first number.
#
# ⚑ THAT PARAGRAPH IS NOW A CHECK, NOT ADVICE (2026-08-03). It sat here as an instruction
# to a person for nine days while the gate compared cargo's DIAGNOSTICS against this list
# — and cargo emits NO diagnostic at all for a unit it never attempts, so a pruned target
# cannot appear on either side of that comparison. Measured on a 3-crate probe
# (`--self-test` R3): breaking `probe-base`'s lib names `probe-base (lib)` and
# `probe-base (lib test)` and NOT ONE WORD about `probe-dep` — neither its lib nor its
# integration test. So allowlisting one red lib would have bought silence over its whole
# cone: `0 new, 0 stale`, green, with an arbitrary number of tests unable to fire (R4).
# `scripts/check-dark-targets.py` now derives the reverse-dependency cone from CARGO'S OWN
# RESOLVE (`cargo metadata`), names every unmeasured package, and WITHHOLDS the staleness
# verdict rather than guessing it. There is deliberately no allowlist row for that state —
# an escape hatch for it is the hole. Repair the lib.
# ⚠ A red lib also prunes ITS OWN bins/tests/examples (they link its rlib), so a dark LIB
# can never be fully written down here: the rows for what it pruned do not exist.
#
# ⚠ Local sweeps see the WORKING TREE; CI sees HEAD. A live lane's uncommitted or
# untracked test file can show up as "dark" locally and is not a row for this list —
# check `git status` on the file before adding it.
#
# Adding a row is a real cost. Say WHY, and name what the dark test was guarding.

# ── THE LIST IS EMPTY (2026-07-25). Every target in the workspace compiles. ──────────
#
# It held TWELVE rows earlier today. The last two to clear were the FRI soundness ledger
# gate (`dregg-circuit-prove` tests `fri_params_soundness_budget` /
# `fri_regrid_post_s2_measure`), dark for five days. The repair took TWO commits and was
# not complete until the second: 3ba423cbc6 restored build.rs (probe + check-cfg + cfg
# emission + shim.define) and lib.rs (`FriKnobs`/`FriLedger`/`fri_ledger`/
# `fri_ledger_available` + the `mod ffi` bridge), which left `dregg_fri_ledger_str`
# DECLARED with no definition anywhere — a link error, not a compile error, so the targets
# stopped being dark while still not running. a954ac5892 added the `lean_init.c` C shim
# that actually reaches the Lean export. Three layers were needed; two looked like enough.
#
# KEEP THE LESSON, not the row. That outage is the reference case for how this file's
# subject matter is created, and it has three parts worth remembering:
#
#   * IT TOOK TWO COMMITS, NEITHER MENTIONING FRI. 7ebe7b7d4b dropped the `dregg_fri_ledger`
#     archive probe + its `rustc-check-cfg` + its `rustc-cfg` emission from build.rs (subject:
#     a PQ-substitution SECURITY STRENGTHENING); 0f2802a0ca, 17h later, deleted the Rust API
#     and the `lean_init.c` C shim. Stage one disarmed the gate SILENTLY; only stage two made
#     it a compile error anyone could see. A commit subject is not a description of a diff.
#
#   * THE SAME REWRITE DROPPED A SECOND GATE, and that one never went dark at all.
#     7ebe7b7d4b removed `dregg_constraint_admits`'s probe/check-cfg/emission/shim.define too
#     — the REALITY-GATE (fbe236f32b) routing the node's admission decision through the Lean
#     constraint evaluator. Because nothing DELETED its Rust API, the `#[cfg]` simply went
#     always-false and `constraint_admits_available()` returned false for 4d17h, compiling
#     green the whole time. It was restored by accident on 07-24 (b01d0a7c1d, a manifest
#     widening), not by anyone noticing. A dark target is the LOUD failure mode; the quiet one
#     leaves no row here at all.
#
#   * THE DETECTOR EXISTED AND WAS OPTED OUT OF. `unexpected_cfgs = "deny"`
#     (`[workspace.lints.rust]`) fires exactly on a `#[cfg(foo)]` whose `foo` no build script
#     declares — it would have caught BOTH drops the moment 7ebe7b7d4b landed. It binds only
#     crates with `[lints] workspace = true`, and `dregg-lean-ffi/Cargo.toml` has no `[lints]`
#     section — the one crate whose entire job is cfg-gating access to verified Lean exports
#     is the crate where an undeclared cfg gate is not an error. (Audited 2026-07-25: all 28
#     `dregg_*_present` cfgs used under `dregg-lean-ffi/src/` are currently declared in its
#     build.rs, so nothing is dangling right now — but nothing STOPS the next one.)
#
# ── DARK FILES: `file ` ROWS (the mod-declaration sweep) ─────────────────────────────
# The ratchet above catches a target that FAILS TO COMPILE. It cannot catch a file rustc
# NEVER OPENS. That file is not a target, so `--keep-going` never names it, no diagnostic
# mentions it, and `cargo test -- <filter over its tests>` prints `0 filtered out … ok` —
# a GREEN report over a run that executed nothing. Both failures leave every `#[test]` in
# the file unable to fire; only one of them is visible.
#
# `scripts/check-dark-modules.py` (run by the `mod-declaration sweep` step of the SAME
# `clippy-correctness` job) sweeps every tracked `.rs` for a reaching `mod` declaration,
# `[[bin]]`/`path =` target root, `build.rs`, or `#[path]`/`include!`. Rows here are
# prefixed `file ` so the two readers partition one list. Same two-sided ratchet: a dark
# file not listed FAILS, a listed file that became reachable FAILS.
#
#     file <path>   # why it is deliberately uncompiled, and who owns it
#
# Reproduce locally:  python3 scripts/check-dark-modules.py --print-dark
#
# ⚠ WHAT THIS CLASS HAS COST, TWICE. `eth-lightclient`'s `bridge_lc_ffi` — the ETH
# light-client verification bridge — had never been compiled, and its own
# `cargo test --lib -- bridge_lc_ffi` matched 0 of 24 tests and reported success. Then
# `sdk/src/fhegg.rs`: `26005d1fe8` (07-17) added it AND its `mod` line and ran its tests
# (3 passed); `b6702625a7` (07-20, "verified ML-DSA sign core INSTALLED") deleted the mod
# line and its six-line comment as collateral in a lib.rs hunk its own file-by-file message
# never mentions. The `fhegg` feature stayed in `default`, so for five days every SDK
# consumer compiled `fhegg-solver` while `dregg_sdk::fhegg` did not exist and its
# tamper-refusal tooth never ran. A file can be wired, tested, and STILL go dark later.
#
# MEASURED at the commit that added this sweep: 3,978 tracked `.rs`, 21 dark. Three were
# real and are now resolved — `circuit/src/xmss.rs` WIRED (15 tests, all green, canaried),
# `sdk/src/fhegg.rs` RE-WIRED, `dregg-dsl/src/gen_diff_test.rs` DELETED (it was RED: three
# E0004s, superseded by `dregg-dsl-differential`). One more was found that the original
# sweep missed and is enumerated below. The other 17 are intentional.

# ── GENUINELY DARK, NOT MINE TO FIX (1) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# 767 lines with 3 `#[test]`s, unreferenced since the repo's root commit (4f736aa709) —
# `deos-js/src/lib.rs` declares its 20-odd sibling cards and `mailtown` (whose own doc says
# it "mirrors the `mud` module") but has never declared `mud`. Same class as `fhegg.rs`,
# found by this sweep and NOT by the `mod`-grep that preceded it. Compile status UNMEASURED
# — stated, not claimed. Owner: the deos-js lane. Wire it or delete it; this row exists so
# it is DETECTED rather than merely documented, not to bless it.
file deos-js/src/mud.rs

# ── NEVER-RUN: `never-run ` ROWS (the execution sweep) ───────────────────────────────
# The compile-fail ratchet catches a target rustc REFUSES. The mod sweep catches a file
# rustc NEVER OPENS. This third sweep catches the quietest one of all: a target that
# compiles, is wired, is named in a manifest — and that NO WORKFLOW CAN EXECUTE.
#
# `scripts/check-never-run-targets.py` (the `execution sweep` step of the SAME
# `clippy-correctness` job) is the reader. Rows are prefixed `never-run ` so all three
# readers partition one list:
#
#     never-run <package> <kind> <name>   # verdict, why, and what would arm it
#
# Reproduce locally:  python3 scripts/check-never-run-targets.py --explain
#
# ⚠ WHY THIS ONE IS WORSE THAN `#[ignore]`. An ignored test at least PRINTS `ignored`.
# These print nothing. Cargo emits no line whatsoever for a target whose
# `required-features` are off — not a skip, not a count, nothing — so a green run is
# indistinguishable from a green run that covered them. A whole-file
# `#![cfg(feature = "x")]` is worse still: the binary is built, executes, and reports
# `test result: ok. 0 passed; 0 failed`, which reads exactly like a passing suite.
#
# ⚠⚠ DO NOT COUNT THESE FROM THE MANIFESTS. The sweep that discovered this population
# did, and reported 32 against a true 63 — wrong in BOTH directions at once. Cargo
# UNIFIES features across a `--workspace` resolve, INCLUDING THROUGH DEV-DEPENDENCIES:
# `dreggnet-market` dev-depends on `dreggnet-catalog` with
# `features = ["private-fhegg-game-consequence"]`, that turns on
# `dreggnet-market/private-attested-clearing`, which turns on `private-clearing` AND
# `fhegg-fhe/amm-input-binding`. So FIFTEEN targets whose manifests say
# `required-features = ["amm-input-binding"]` / `["private-clearing"]` — counted as dark
# by the hand sweep — are ACTIVE on every `cargo test --workspace` and always were.
# Conversely `lean-seed.yml` passes `--features lean-lib`, which arms nothing, because it
# is a `cargo run` and `cargo build/run --bin` never compiles a test target. The oracle
# is CARGO'S OWN RESOLVE, and a `required-features` line is not evidence in either
# direction.
#
# THE VERDICT IS PER-ROW AND THE THREE ANSWERS DIFFER. "Expensive" wants a nightly.
# "Environment" wants a seeded runner or an honest, PRINTED skip. "Forgotten" wants
# nothing but the wiring, and every row under that heading is a guard that could be
# green this week. Do not apply one policy to all of them.

# ── EXPENSIVE (28): real recursion folds, FHE, or MPC-TLS 2PC. A nightly, not a push. ─
# These are the class `armed-teeth.yml` already exists for: minutes-to-hours of genuine
# proving. Putting them on the per-push gate is how the gate gets deleted. The residual
# is that no nightly arms them YET — `armed-teeth.yml` covers `dregg-circuit-prove`'s
# `#[ignore]`d teeth only, and these are gated by FEATURE rather than by `#[ignore]`, so
# `--run-ignored` cannot reach them. Owner: the crate named in each row.
never-run dreggnet-party test away_team   # `private-role-assignment` links the heavy proof PRODUCER (dregg-circuit-prove + plonky3).
never-run dreggnet-market test dark_amm_collective_session   # `dark-amm-game`: BFV producer/verifier boundary + HidingFri tower.
never-run dreggnet-market test dark_amm_collective_worker   # `dark-amm-game`, ditto — the multi-process worker half.
never-run dreggnet-market test dark_amm_game   # `dark-amm-game`, ditto.
never-run dreggnet-market test dark_amm_private_tool   # `dark-amm-game`, ditto.
never-run dreggnet-market test dark_amm_proved_game   # `dark-amm-game`, ditto — the PROVED variant, the most expensive of the set.
never-run dreggnet-market test dark_amm_same_opening_game   # `dark-amm-game`, ditto.
never-run dreggnet-market test dark_amm_same_opening_tool   # `dark-amm-game`, ditto.
never-run dreggnet-web test dark_amm_game   # `dark-amm-game` through the web adapter; same tower.
never-run dreggnet-web test dark_amm_proved_game   # `dark-amm-game` through the web adapter; same tower.
never-run dreggnet-web test fhegg_operation   # `fhegg-settlement` pulls the full TFHE stack (its own manifest says so).
never-run dreggnet-web test private_raid_operation   # `private-raid-operation` = real HidingFri-backed raid assignment.
never-run dreggnet-web test private_preference_operation   # `private-preference-operation`, same HidingFri tower.
never-run dreggnet-web test private_fair_shuffle_operation   # `private-fair-shuffle-operation`, same HidingFri tower.
never-run dreggnet-web test private_quest_operation   # `private-quest-operation`, same HidingFri tower.
never-run dreggnet-web test private_chat_affordances   # needs THREE of the private-operation towers at once.
never-run dreggnet-web test private_operation_no_viewer   # `private-preference-operation`; the no-viewer boundary assertion.
never-run dreggnet-web test private_operation_web_boundary   # needs three private-operation towers at once.
never-run dreggnet-web test public_shielded_games   # `public-shielded-games` pulls every completed mechanic's owning verifier stack.
never-run fhegg-fhe test tfhe_high_level_wgpu   # `tfhe-integer` compiles tfhe-rs 1.6 (a monster) AND wants a GPU adapter. See ENVIRONMENT note below.
never-run fhegg-fhe test tfhe_wgpu_blind_rotation   # `tfhe-integer`, ditto.
never-run fhegg-fhe test tfhe_wgpu_cmux   # `tfhe-integer`, ditto.
never-run fhegg-fhe test tfhe_wgpu_ntt_crossover   # `tfhe-integer`, ditto.
never-run fhegg-fhe test tfhe_wgpu_parity   # `tfhe-integer`, ditto.
never-run fhegg-fhe test tfhe_wgpu_pbs_deployed_envelope   # `tfhe-integer`, ditto.
never-run fhegg-fhe test tfhe_wgpu_pbs_extract_keyswitch   # `tfhe-integer`, ditto.
#
# ⚠ THE SEVEN `tfhe-*` ROWS ARE STILL DARK (no lane enables `tfhe-integer`), but the
# SELF-SKIPPING-TEST polarity IS FIXED — re-verified at HEAD 2026-08-05: the shape this
# note used to describe, `if std::env::var_os("DREGG_REQUIRE_WGPU").is_none() {
# eprintln!("skipped"); return; }`, now occurs ZERO times across all seven files.
# THREE of them (`tfhe_high_level_wgpu`, `tfhe_wgpu_ntt_crossover`,
# `tfhe_wgpu_pbs_deployed_envelope`) took the `ristretto_*_wgpu_required` shape:
# `#[ignore]` + a HARD `assert!(env::var_os("DREGG_REQUIRE_WGPU").is_some(), ...)`, so an
# opted-in lane cannot hollowly pass and a GPU-less lane skips EXPLICITLY.
# The other FOUR (`tfhe_wgpu_blind_rotation`, `_cmux`, `_parity`,
# `_pbs_extract_keyswitch`) are NOT `#[ignore]`d: they assert bit-exactness against a CPU
# oracle and select `TorusMacPolicy::Auto` unless `DREGG_REQUIRE_WGPU` is set, LABELLING a
# `CpuFallback` rather than skipping. Read those four honestly: they are real parity
# tests, but on a GPU-less box they compare CPU against tfhe-rs CPU and prove nothing
# about a kernel. Only `DREGG_REQUIRE_WGPU=1` on a box with a real adapter makes them
# device-bearing.

# ── ENVIRONMENT (12): needs a seeded runner, an adapter, or a runtime CI does not have. ─
# The right answer here is a seeded runner where one is affordable, and an HONEST,
# PRINTED skip where it is not — never silence.
#
# FOUR ROWS WERE HERE AND ARE NOW ARMED INSTEAD OF LISTED. `dregg-lean-ffi`'s
# `handler_cutover_probe`, `deployed_constraint_probe`, `multiway_tug_oracle_probe` and
# `embeddable_runtime_probe_linux` needed a linked `libdregg_lean.a` — and ci.yml's
# `lean-marshal-gate` job already FETCHES one. The environment was not missing; nobody
# had pointed a `--test` at them. They now run there, under an assertion-count floor of
# 18, because every one of them reports `ok. 0 passed` rather than failing when its cfg
# is off. "Needs an environment" is a verdict to CHECK, not to assume: three of these
# four cost nothing but a line.
never-run fhegg-fhe test party_mpc_certified_preprocessing   # `verified-pq-runtime-tests` links dregg-lean-ffi for the Lean-verified ML-DSA cores, and re-execs itself as a child process.
never-run fhegg-fhe test party_mpc_preprocessing_use   # `verified-pq-runtime-tests`, ditto.
never-run fhegg-fhe test distributed_threshold_committee   # `verified-pq-runtime-tests`; spawns THREE party processes + a relying party via CARGO_BIN_EXE.
never-run fhegg-fhe test distributed_netting_processes   # `verified-pq-runtime-tests`, ditto — the separate-OS-process distributed netting demonstrator (added 2026-07-26 in f84cee425, under the same already-dark gate as the three rows above it; it was never runnable, not newly un-run).
#
# ⚑ 2026-08-07: THE NINE `deos-hermes` ROWS BELOW CARRIED THE WRONG REASON, AND IT WAS THE
# KIND THIS BLOCK'S OWN HEADING WARNS ABOUT — an assumed verdict, not a checked one. Each
# said "the mozjs elephant". MEASURED, at HEAD, the elephant is ALREADY PAID FOR NIGHTLY,
# ON THE SAME RUNNER:
#
#   * `starbridge-v2/Cargo.toml:163-171` — `desktop` includes `agent-js`;
#     `:287` — `agent-js = ["embedded-executor", "dep:deos-js"]`;
#     `:215` — `native-full = ["desktop"]`.
#     So `armed-teeth.yml`'s `gpui-gated-desktop-teeth` job, which runs
#     `cargo test -p starbridge-v2 --features native-full` on hbox every night, builds
#     deos-js AND SpiderMonkey already. mozjs is not a reason for these rows to be dark;
#     it is a cost this repository elects to pay on a schedule.
#   * `starbridge-v2/Cargo.toml:312` — `live-brain = ["agent-js", "dep:deos-hermes",
#     "deos-hermes/js-agent"]`. The feature these nine rows are gated on is REACHABLE from
#     the root graph; nothing merely "excludes" it.
#   * mozjs builds on the developer box too: `target/debug/build/mozjs_sys-*/out/build/`
#     holds `libjsapi.a` + `libjsglue.a`, rebuilt 2026-08-06.
#   Confirmed by RESOLVE, not by reading feature names:
#   `cd starbridge-v2 && cargo tree --features native-full -i deos-js` -> `deos-js <-
#   starbridge-v2`; `-i mozjs` -> `mozjs v0.15.7 <- deos-js`.
#
#   ⚠ CAVEAT, NOT ROUNDED AWAY: deos-hermes is a standalone workspace pinning
#   `mozjs 0.15.14` / `mozjs_sys 140.10.1-0`, while that resolve is `0.15.7` / `0.140.8-2`.
#   Arming these does not REUSE the nightly SpiderMonkey; it builds a second one in
#   `deos-hermes/target`. Proven: the toolchain, prerequisites and disk are present and
#   exercised nightly. Unifying the two mozjs pins is a lockfile edit if the duplicate cost
#   is worth removing.
#
# ⚠ THE REAL BLOCKER, AND IT IS SHARED WITH THREE OTHER RED LANES. `deos-hermes` depends on
# `dregg-sdk` with DEFAULT features, which embed the verified Lean executor (its own
# manifest header says so and calls it deliberate). On 2026-08-07 the seed for HEAD's Lean
# tree does not exist: `dregg-lean-ffi/lean-seed.pin` pins `DREGG_TREE_HASH=406424cf…`
# against a checkout of `2b72ef82…`, the derived asset
# `libdregg_lean-Linux-x86_64-v4.30.0-d9a5c5465cb75c79.a.zst` is absent from the release's
# 152 published assets, and `dregg-lean-ffi/build.rs:2569` then refuses to substitute an
# older archive. That single absence is ALSO why `armed-teeth.yml`'s `lean-hard-mode`
# (curl 404), `feature-gated-prove-teeth` (0 of 4) and `binding-teeth` (0 of 17) were all
# red on 2026-08-07. Publish a seed for HEAD and these nine become a `--test` line.
#
# ⚠ WHAT IS NOT MEASURED, said plainly rather than implied: nobody has compiled
# `deos-hermes --features js-agent` at HEAD. These rows record that the target is NEVER
# RUN, which is exactly true; they do not assert it would pass, or even compile. The
# invocation that would settle it is
# `cd deos-hermes && cargo test --features js-agent --test <name>`.

# ⚠ PLATFORM DARKNESS, WHICH THIS SWEEP CANNOT SEE AND WHICH ALREADY COST.
# `scripts/check-lean-marshal.sh` (ci.yml's `lean-marshal-gate`) arms exactly two of
# dregg-lean-ffi's whole-file `#![cfg(feature = "lean-lib")]` probes by name:
# `embeddable_runtime_probe` and `overspend_probe`. The rest are armed by that job's
# `Lean runtime probes nothing else builds` step, which now names TEN of them (2026-08-08:
# the four it carried plus poa_dark_bazaar_judge / poa_records / poa_signal_feedback /
# poa_slot_derive / poa_station_daily / trustline_step_oracle, all six of which this sweep
# was reporting UNLISTED) — but `embeddable_runtime_probe` is ALSO
# `#![cfg(target_os = "macos")]` and that job runs on `ubuntu-latest`, so it has reported
# `ok. 0 passed` on every CI run since it was wired, while `embeddable_runtime_probe_linux`
# — the Linux twin written precisely for that runner — was named by nothing at all. One
# probe runs empty, its twin never ran, and the gate was green. This sweep keys on
# FEATURES, not on the runner's OS, so it can see the twin and not the empty one. Stated,
# not hidden.

# ── ENVIRONMENT / PLATFORM (4) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
never-run starbridge-web test pty_ws_e2e   # `pty-ws-server`: a real PTY + websocket server end to end.

# ⚑ THE ONE OF THE 2026-08-08 EIGHT THAT IS NOT WIRING (decided per target, not by class).
# `linked_archive_freshness` compares each `Dregg2_<Mod>.o` member's `ar` mtime against the
# mtime of `metatheory/Dregg2/<Mod>.lean`. `actions/checkout` DOES NOT PRESERVE MTIMES — it
# writes every source file at checkout time — while a fetched seed archive's members carry
# the stamps of the box that built it, necessarily earlier. So on any hosted runner EVERY
# resolvable member reads stale past the 120s rounding slack and the test fails by
# construction, no matter how fresh the seed is. That is a check that CANNOT PASS there, and
# requiring one is how an escape hatch becomes routine — it is a real gate on a box that
# BUILT the archive, and a wall anywhere else. Do NOT "fix" it by raising
# AR_MTIME_RESOLUTION_SLACK_SECS; the file says so itself and it would be a staleness budget.
# WHAT COVERS THE SAME QUESTION IN CI'S ABSENCE, verified present at this commit rather than
# relayed: `scripts/check-lean-seed-member-freshness.py`, which asks the identical per-member
# question of the SEED at a fixed path with no cargo and no mtimes-from-checkout, and has two
# rows in `scripts/local-gates.sh` (`lean-seed-member-freshness` and its
# `lean-seed-member-freshness-red` `--self-test`). Its second `#[test]`,
# `the_freshness_reader_can_go_red`, is pure strings + a scratch temp tree and would pass
# anywhere; it is not separable from the target. Owner: dregg-lean-ffi.
never-run dregg-lean-ffi test linked_archive_freshness   # `lean-lib` + an archive whose members postdate a checkout: unreachable on a hosted runner by construction (see the block above). Seed-side twin: scripts/check-lean-seed-member-freshness.py, in local-gates.sh.

# ── DEFAULT-FEATURE FALLOUT (14): these RAN on every push until 2026-07-27. ───────────
# ⚑ THIS HEADING IS A COVERAGE REGRESSION, NOT A STANDING COST, and it is the only one
# here that used to be green. `ba3d84301` changed `starbridge-v2`'s default from
# `["desktop"]` to `["embedded-executor"]` — correctly, and for a well-measured reason:
# `starbridge-v2` is a root workspace member, cargo UNIFIES features across a
# `--workspace` resolve, and its ten-switch default was silently rewriting 60 other
# packages (153 leave the resolve entirely) and overruling nine consumers' explicit
# `default-features = false`. That commit is right and should stand.
#
# What it did NOT do is notice these. Its own body states "`.github/dark-targets.txt` is
# unaffected: it is empty, and a `required-features` target that is simply not activated
# was never one of its rows." Both halves are wrong: this file holds 56 `never-run` rows,
# and "a target whose gate no invocation activates" is EXACTLY this sweep's subject — it
# is the third sweep, added 2026-07-26 in 73e3b9b0d, one day before. So the twelve
# starbridge-v2 file-gated tests and the two servo-render `libservo` tests went from
# running on every `cargo test --workspace` to running nowhere, and the commit that did
# it recorded the compile-time saving and not the falsifiers.
#
# WHAT ARMS THEM TODAY, AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH: `starbridge-v2-installers.yml`
# (`push: branches: [main]`, no paths filter) gained
# `cargo test --release --features desktop --no-run`. That is a REAL and deliberate
# improvement over the accidental default — rustc reads every line and a compile error
# fails the push — but `--no-run` builds the binaries and executes none of them, so
# every assertion inside is still a falsifier that cannot fire. The gate is right to
# call that never-run.
#
# ⚑ OWNER: ember. The open decision is whether the cockpit/desktop suite is worth
# EXECUTING per-push (gpui + servo + stylo + webrender is the elephant that job already
# carries once, so the marginal cost is the run, not the build) or whether these belong
# on a nightly. Dropping `--no-run` from that one step is the whole arming change; it is
# not made here because it is a CI-budget call, not a wiring omission.
#
# ── PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-07-31: the NIGHTLY branch of that fork, for four of them ──
# `armed-teeth.yml`'s `gpui-gated-desktop-teeth` job now RUNS four of these on the
# self-hosted host (hbox), floored on what actually executed. Their rows are gone from
# this list because the two-sided ratchet requires it: a row that became executable
# fails just as loudly as one that never ran. The four:
#     deos_desktop_transclude_is_verified   (new; the flagship anti-forge tooth)
#     deos_desktop_conflict_is_a_state
#     deos_desktop_editor_types_to_heap
#     deos_desktop_world_explorer_and_spotter
#     two_instance_multiplayer_session              (the umem carry tooth, below)
#     branch_stitch_settlement_sound_multiplayer    (ditto)
#
# ⚑ WHY THE LAST TWO, specifically. `starbridge-v2/src/umem_membrane.rs`'s
# `open_umem_envelope` is the anti-substitution tooth on the umem carry path: it refuses
# an envelope whose re-derived root does not match BOTH the expected root and the
# envelope's own claim. It has ZERO production callers — every caller in the tree is a
# test — and its only two callers OUTSIDE its own `mod tests` were these two targets,
# which never ran. So the carry tooth was exercised nowhere a CI or nightly could see.
# (`grain-fork` does consume the module, but the STITCH half — `stitch_projections` /
# `settle_umem_stitch` — not the carry path; `deos-matrix` only names it in a comment.)
# Both were measured green before arming.
#
# ── AND THREE MORE ARMED 2026-08-01, WHICH NEVER HAD ROWS HERE AT ALL ────────────────
# `deos_desktop_composer_has_a_real_entry_point`, `deos_desktop_stitcher_is_the_conflict_surface`
# and `deos_desktop_composes_a_doc_from_cells` landed AFTER the six above were armed,
# carrying the same `#![cfg(all(feature = "gpui-ui", feature = "embedded-executor"))]`.
# They were therefore never-run FROM BIRTH and were never triaged into this file at all —
# `scripts/check-never-run-targets.py` reported all three as NEW NEVER-RUN, which is the
# ratchet doing the one job no row could have done for it. All three are now ARMED in
# `gpui-gated-desktop-teeth` (floor raised 6 -> 10 for their 1+1+2 tests), measured green
# on the real feature set BEFORE arming. Recorded here rather than silently absent,
# because the count a reader takes off this heading is otherwise wrong about what the
# nightly actually covers.
#
# The SEVEN below are still the open CI-budget call, unchanged. Per-push execution was
# NOT chosen for them; adding one to the nightly job is a one-line `--test` and a floor
# bump.
#
# ⚠ AND THE SWEEP ITSELF WAS LYING ABOUT THIS BLOCK, in a way that cancelled out. Until
# 2026-07-31 `check-never-run-targets.py` compared `--features` LITERALLY (so an alias
# like `native-full` never satisfied a `gpui-ui` gate) AND did not model `--no-run` (so a
# compile-only invocation was credited with arming). Two errors in opposite directions.
# Fixing only the first made ALL ELEVEN of these read "NO LONGER NEVER-RUN" on the
# strength of `starbridge-v2-installers.yml`'s `--no-run` step — a false green inside the
# sweep whose entire job is catching false greens. Both fixes landed together.
